title: GCP Pub/Sub: `subscriptionSize` is announced for removal in 2.20 — use `mode` and `value`

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **GCP Pub/Sub Scaler**: The `subscriptionSize` setting is DEPRECATED and will be removed in v2.20 - Use `mode` and `value` instead (#6866)
remediation: On each gcp-pubsub trigger named, replace `subscriptionSize: N` with `mode: SubscriptionSize` and `value: N`. 2.18 only logs a KEDAScalerInfo event; 2.20 refuses the trigger.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "gcp-pubsub") and (.metadata // {} | has("subscriptionSize"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is refused by the 2.20 scaler

title: RabbitMQ: `queueLength` is deprecated — use `mode: QueueLength` and `value`

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: DEPRECATED: please use `mode: QueueLength` and `v…** — `queueLength` - **DEPRECATED: please use `mode: QueueLength` and `value: ##` instead**. Defines a threshold value for the queue length passed to the scaler. For example: if one pod can handle 10 messages, set the queue length target to `10`. If the actual number of messages in the queue is 30, the scaler will scale up to 3 pods. Default is set to `20` unless `publishRate` is specified, in which case `queueLength` is disabled for this trigger.
remediation: Docs-only deprecation (no CHANGELOG entry, no struct tag yet): on each rabbitmq trigger named replace `queueLength: N` with `mode: QueueLength` + `value: N`. The old key keeps working on every 2.x release.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "rabbitmq") and (.metadata // {} | has("queueLength"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row still uses the deprecated key

title: keda-admission-webhooks: the deprecated Prometheus metric names are removed

detection.reason: which metric names a dashboard or alert reads from the webhook's /metrics endpoint is not in the collected projection

remediation: Alerts or dashboards on the admission webhook's old `keda_webhook_*` metric names stop matching after this hop; move them to the current names exposed by keda-admission-webhooks.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules.monitoring.coreos.com -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.groups[]?.rules[]?.expr | test("keda_webhook_")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a rule file that reads a webhook metric; check its name against the 2.18 endpoint

title: cpu / memory triggers: `type` is removed — the scaler refuses the trigger

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **CPU Memory scaler**: The `type` setting is deprecated and removed, use `metricType` instead (#6698)
remediation: pkg/scalers/cpu_memory_scaler.go tags `type` as `deprecated=` at v2.18.0, and the typed-config parser turns a present deprecated parameter into an error — every ScaledObject / ScaledJob named stops scaling after the hop ("scaler cpu info: The 'type' setting is DEPRECATED and is removed in v2.18"). Delete `metadata.type` and set the trigger-level `metricType` before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "cpu" or .type == "memory") and (.metadata // {} | has("type"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is refused by the 2.18 scaler

title: GCP Pub/Sub, Stackdriver and Cloud Tasks triggers are deprecated (Google retired MQL)

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: name=filter, order=triggerMetadata, deprecatedAnnounce=This scaler is deprecated. More info -> 'https://keda.sh/blog/2025-09-15-gcp-deprecations'
remediation: From v2.18.0 these three scalers carry a deprecatedAnnounce tag (keda.sh/blog/2025-09-15-gcp-deprecations): they rely on Google Cloud's Monitoring Query Language, receive no further changes, and will be removed if Google drops MQL. Each ScaledObject / ScaledJob named keeps working on this hop; plan the move to the `prometheus` trigger against Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus (`gcp-storage` is unaffected). This deprecation is NOT in CHANGELOG.md — only the struct tags and the blog carry it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select(.type == "gcp-pubsub" or .type == "gcp-stackdriver" or .type == "gcp-cloudtasks") | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row uses an MQL-based trigger KEDA no longer develops

title: Admission webhook: adopting an existing HPA now requires naming it in `advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name`

detection.reason: the rejection concerns a ScaledObject being CREATED for a workload that already has a hand-written HPA — a future object, not one in the snapshot

quote: the existing hpa '%s' for workload '%s' of type '%s' must be specified by name in advanced settings to enable ownership transfer
remediation: From 2.18 a new ScaledObject whose target already has a HorizontalPodAutoscaler is rejected unless `spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name` names that HPA — KEDA then takes ownership of it instead of fighting it. Nothing in place changes; tell app teams migrating HPAs to ScaledObjects after the upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl get hpa -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.metadata.labels // {})["scaledobject.keda.sh/name"] == null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) -> \(.spec.scaleTargetRef.kind)/\(.spec.scaleTargetRef.name)"'  # each row is an HPA KEDA does not own; a ScaledObject created for its target must name it
